title: Patch: the AI's trade reckoning counts a Reborn unit's return, so killing one is not priced as removing it

**Issue #1796 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #1796: Patch: the AI's trade reckoning counts a Reborn unit's return, so killing one is not priced as removing it
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
A unit with Reborn comes back once after it dies, at 1 health. When the practice AI weighs an attack, and when it imagines how its opponent will attack next turn, it treats killing a Reborn unit as if the unit were gone for good. For example, killing a 5/5 Reborn is priced as a full kill, though it comes straight back as a 5/1. So the AI overvalues spending attacks on Reborn units and expects its opponent to do the same, which can steer it away from a better kill or from attacking the hero. Once built, a kill is worth what it really removes.

## Why
- `crates/ai/src/reply.rs:109-119` (`trade_value`) credits a kill with `unit_worth(target)` in full, and charges a dying attacker `unit_worth(attacker)` in full. Neither looks at Reborn.
- `unit_worth` (`evaluate.rs:104-127`) even adds the Reborn keyword's own weight (`reborn: 2.0`, `config.rs:436`) to the kill's credit.
- `trade_value` decides two things:
  - the order of the opponent model's attacks (`ranked_attacks`, `reply.rs:140-167`);
  - the AI's own even-trade pick from #1779 (`even_trade`, `candidates.rs:312-319`).
- The crate already models the return elsewhere. The Taunt-wall walk brings a destroyed Reborn neighbour back through `reborn_body` (`evaluate.rs:654-666` and `752-760`, §4.5 step 4, reset at `REBORN_HEALTH`).

## Proposal
- Split `reborn_body` so the returned body is available without its Taunt condition (for example `reborn_return(state, unit)`), keeping the Taunt filter at its existing call site.
- In `trade_value`, when a strike kills a target whose Reborn is unspent, credit `unit_worth(target) - unit_worth(returned body)`.
- Do the same for an attacker with unspent Reborn that dies.
- Every number stays an existing weight (CLAUDE.md rule 9).

## Where it lands
- `crates/ai/src/reply.rs`, `crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs`
- `crates/ai/tests/ai/reply.rs`, `crates/ai/tests/ai/even_trades.rs`
- `crates/ai/README.md` where it describes the static trader
- §4.5 step 4 (Reborn), §9.9 (the AI)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Unit test: the opponent holds a 6/6, and the seat holds a Reborn 5/5 and a vanilla 4/4. The simulated reply kills the 4/4.
- [ ] Unit test: `trade_value` for killing a Reborn unit equals its worth minus the worth of its 1-health return. With Reborn already spent, it is the full worth.
- [ ] An `even_trades.rs` case: given two targets with equal stats, the AI's even-trade pick prefers the one without Reborn.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo jackioh gate` pass.
- [ ] An improve-dev screen (`training/improve.md`, "A screen": 400 games against the parent build) is run, and its result is reported in the pull request whatever it reads.

## Size and risks
Small: about 20 lines plus tests. The reply model feeds the evaluation, so every game moves a little. The screen guards against a loss.
```
